title: He Took No Upfront Fee. Four Days Later, Akshay Kumar Is Laughing All the Way Past ₹100 Crore.
excerpt: Welcome to the Jungle crosses ₹106 crore worldwide in four days — and Akshay's profit-sharing gamble is starting to look like the smartest deal in Bollywood.
body:
There's a scene early in **Welcome to the Jungle** where **Akshay Kumar**'s character finds himself surrounded on all sides, outnumbered and outgunned, with nothing but timing and nerve. It might as well be a metaphor for the last three years of his career.

But something has shifted. The man who spent the better part of 2023 and 2024 watching his films tank — *Selfiee*, *OMG 2*, *Mission Raniganj*, one after another — has now delivered four consecutive ₹100 crore grossers in under twelve months. **Sky Force**. **Housefull 5**. **Bhooth Bangla**, which sailed past ₹200 crore. And now Welcome to the Jungle, which crossed **₹106 crore worldwide in just four days**, making it Bollywood's most expensive comedy ever mounted and, increasingly, one of the surest bets of the year.

## The Numbers That Tell the Story

The franchise's third instalment opened to **₹15.25 crore** on Friday — boosted by paid previews that added ₹3.75 crore — and climbed steadily through the weekend: ₹20 crore on Saturday, ₹24 crore on Sunday. Monday brought the usual weekday dip to ₹8 crore, but that's still a remarkably strong hold for a comedy without a holiday cushion. The four-day India nett stands at approximately **₹71 crore**, tracking **13% ahead of Bhooth Bangla** at the same stage. Overseas, the film has added roughly **₹17 crore (around $1.75 million)**, pushing the worldwide gross past the century mark.

For diaspora audiences who grew up quoting Nana Patekar and Anil Kapoor lines from the original, these numbers land differently. Welcome (2007) and Welcome Back (2015) were NRI staples — the kind of films you watched on family movie nights in Edison and Brampton and Southall. The third instalment swaps the original mob bosses for a new jungle-set chaos, but the audience has clearly showed up for the brand.

## Akshay's Smartest Gamble

Here's the detail that makes this story genuinely interesting: **Akshay Kumar didn't take an upfront acting fee**.

Instead, according to multiple trade reports, he negotiated a **backend profit-sharing deal** — a model where his payday is directly tied to how much the film earns. On a ₹125 crore budget (roughly ₹60 crore for production, ₹35 crore for the ensemble cast, the rest for crew and promotion), that's a significant risk. If the film flopped, he'd walk away with a fraction of his usual ₹50-80 crore fee.

But Welcome to the Jungle isn't flopping. If it follows the Bhooth Bangla trajectory — which added roughly ₹48 crore after its second week — the film should sail past ₹120 crore India nett, which would make it a clean **HIT** on its budget. And with satellite, digital, and music rights likely pre-sold at premium, Akshay's profit share could end up dwarfing any upfront fee he's ever commanded.

> "Thank you is very small," Akshay wrote on social media this week, bowing in gratitude to veteran co-stars **Farida Jalal** and **Kiran Kumar** — a gesture that felt less like a publicity move and more like a man who knows he's riding something real.

## What's Working (and What's Not)

Director **Ahmed Khan** has leaned into parody and spoof territory this time, which is a departure from the broad family comedy that made the first two films universal. The treatment works for the multiplexes, but it's also limiting the film's reach. The absence of **Uday and Majnu** — the beloved characters played by Nana Patekar and Anil Kapoor — hasn't gone unnoticed either. What the film has instead is sheer volume: **Suniel Shetty**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Paresh Rawal**, **Johnny Lever**, **Rajpal Yadav**, **Sanjay Dutt**, **Jackie Shroff**, **Disha Patani**, **Jacqueline Fernandez**, **Raveena Tandon**, and **Lara Dutta** all crammed into two hours of escalating absurdity.

The Hindi belt states — Rajasthan, UP, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh — are where the film is really overperforming, running significantly ahead of Bhooth Bangla in those territories. Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR are holding steady, though the latter lost some ground to **Carry On Jatta 4**, which continues to dominate East Punjab.

## The Real Test Comes Next

The challenge is right around the corner. **Dhamaal 4** — another beloved franchise comedy with **Ajay Devgn** and ensemble — arrives on July 10. That's a direct collision with Welcome's audience, and it'll determine whether the film finishes as a success or a proper blockbuster. For now, the trade consensus is that Welcome needs to add roughly ₹48-50 crore after its second week to cross the profitability line. Everything depends on how the weekdays hold.

But step back for a moment. A year ago, Akshay Kumar was Bollywood's favourite punchline — the guy who released six films a year and watched all of them sink. Now he's four-for-four in 2025-26, he's reinvented his deal structure, he's picking the right franchises, and he just crossed ₹100 crore worldwide in four days.

Whatever you think of the film, the comeback is undeniable. And if those backend profits start rolling in, don't be surprised when every other A-lister in Mumbai starts asking their agents about the Akshay Kumar model.

**Where to watch:** Currently in theatres across India, the US, UK, Canada, UAE, and Australia. Available in Hindi with English subtitles at most major chains including AMC, Regal, Cineplex, and Odeon.
